related_questions.question: How many times can one have COVID?
related_questions.snippet: People can be reinfected with SARS-CoV-2 multiple times. Each time a person is infected with SARS-CoV-2, they have a risk of developing Long COVID. Long COVID symptoms and conditions can emerge, persist, resolve, and reemerge over weeks and months.

related_questions.question: How bad is COVID now if you get it?
related_questions.snippet: Many people with COVID-19, also called coronavirus disease 2019, recover at home. But for some, COVID-19 can be a serious illness. Some people may need care in the hospital, treatment in the intensive care unit and the need for breathing help.
related_questions.title: COVID-19: Who's at higher risk of serious symptoms? - Mayo Clinic

related_questions.question: How long does COVID last in your body?

text_blocks.snippet: COVID-19 can last in your body for varying durations, ranging from a few weeks to potentially years. While most people recover within a couple of weeks, some experience lingering symptoms or long COVID, which can persist for months or even years.
snippet_highlighted_words: a few weeks to potentially years

list.snippet: Typical recovery: Most individuals recover within a couple of weeks.
Long COVID: Some individuals experience ongoing symptoms or conditions that can last for weeks, months, or even years after the initial infection, according to the CDC.
Lingering virus: An average person might shed the virus for about a month after infection.
Positive tests: Some individuals may continue to test positive for COVID-19 for at least three months, even after symptoms have resolved.
Potential for long-term presence: New studies suggest that the virus might linger in the body for 14 months to two years, even after symptoms disappear.
